name: Alitu
tagline: Clean, assemble, publish, and package a recurring spoken-word podcast episode

tiers.name: Podcaster
tiers.limits: 1 podcast; editing, cleanup, transcription, publishing and hosting; hosting includes 1,000 downloads/month
tiers.notes: Live annual promotion is $247/year ($20.58/month); the normal annual offer is described as 2 months free, equivalent to $31.67/month.

tiers.name: Done-for-you editing
tiers.limits: Professional recurring episode editing; exact episode-frequency and length allowance depends on the selected service
tiers.notes: Starts at $295/month; first month is promoted at $1.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for Podcaster; 30-day money-back guarantee
pricing.hiddenCosts: Hosting above 1,000 downloads/month costs $10/month up to 10,000 downloads; a second podcast normally doubles the subscription, with a discounted two-show price available.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Alitu, clean, assemble, publish, and package a recurring spoken-word podcast episode. The hard boundary is production automation, hosting integrations, support, and creator-specific polish, plus audio infrastructure, distribution, and production polish.
coreLoopDIY: Import spoken-word audio, perform practical cleanup, assemble a recurring podcast episode, and export production files plus show notes.
whatYouLose: production automation, hosting integrations, support, and creator-specific polish
moatNotes: audio infrastructure, distribution, and production polish
ongoingBurden: codec support, loudness standards, transcription, storage, feeds, analytics, and deliverability to directories
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Alitu because creators pay to remove fragile audio plumbing and publishing chores from a release schedule. The recurring cost buys codec support, loudness standards, transcription, storage, feeds, analytics, and deliverability to directories, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Audacity
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source multitrack audio editor and useful implementation prior art.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Audacity
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Edits audio, but does not publish or package the recurring show.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Podcaster plan and a single-creator production tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Alitu in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, ffmpeg, SQLite, and an HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import spoken-word audio, perform practical cleanup, assemble a recurring podcast episode, and export production files plus show notes.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create an upload queue and preserve originals in a read-only media folder.
Generate waveforms and non-destructive edit markers instead of rewriting source files.
Implement silence trimming, loudness normalization to -16 LUFS, fades, and noise-gate presets.
Add chapter markers, intro and outro slots, and a simple two-track timeline.
Produce a transcript and draft title, description, chapters, and social excerpts.
Export MP3, WAV, transcript, chapters JSON, and a complete project manifest.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out real-time remote recording.
Deliberately leave out podcast hosting and directory analytics.
Deliberately leave out licensed stock music and voice cloning.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
